verdict: PINNED (all 3). Admin dir names recorded below. NOT-SAFE for removal of any of the three; gd2d is also ineligible for pruning as a lane (6 unpushed commits).

critical_finding.summary: git worktree prune has NO path selector. It is repo-wide and all-or-nothing: `git worktree prune -n -v` in game-dev-2d-shokunin lists ALL FIVE registrations, the 3 must-survive pins included. A 'selective prune' is therefore not expressible as a filtered `git worktree prune`; the parent must either exclude the 3 pins from the operation or run one registration-level command per doomed worktree.
critical_finding.cli_ground_truth: git --version = 2.55.0; `git worktree prune -h` -> 'usage: git worktree prune [-n] [-v] [--expire <expire>]' — only -n/-v/--expire, no <worktree> argument, unlike `git worktree remove [-f] <worktree>` and `git worktree lock [--reason <string>] <worktree>` which both take a path.
critical_finding.does_not_remove_refs: Pruning a registration deletes the admin dir only; it never deletes refs/heads/wt-r98|wt-r99|wt-r100 or their commits. The residual risk is losing the only pointer that records which checkout the branch was materialised in, and the uncommitted-state evidence (index/ORIG_HEAD/reflog) for 3 branches that hold unpushed work.

mechanism_a_lock.effect: Writes .git/worktrees/<name>/locked; a locked registration is never pruned, so `git worktree prune` (even without --expire) skips it. Reversible with `git worktree unlock`.
mechanism_a_lock.empirically_verified: YES, on an isolated /tmp fixture (git 2.55.0): created wt-keep + wt-drop, deleted both dirs, `git worktree lock --reason pin-audit <wt-keep>` -> exit 0 and locked file present; `git worktree prune -v` -> exit 0, removed wt-drop, wt-keep survived and now lists as 'locked pin-audit'.
mechanism_a_lock.caveat: This MUTATES the gd2d repo's git state (creates a locked file), so per this seat's read-only mandate it was NOT run against the fleet; the parent must execute it if that route is chosen.

mechanism_b_remove_by_path.effect: Removes exactly ONE registration by path, leaving the 3 pins untouched. Works on an ABSENT worktree (the path is already gone), so this is the working form of a 'selective prune' here.
mechanism_b_remove_by_path.empirically_verified: YES, on the same isolated fixture: `git worktree remove <wt-drop>` on the already-deleted dir -> exit 0, that registration gone, wt-keep still registered.
mechanism_b_remove_by_path.caveat: Also mutates git state; not run against the fleet. Targets would be the two UNPINNED registrations only: /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/r80-baseline-frozen-worktree and /tmp/r81-frozen.

mechanism_c_expire_window.effect: --expire filters by the mtime of each admin dir's 'gitdir' file, so it CAN currently separate the two sets.
mechanism_c_expire_window.empirical_split: gitdir mtimes: r80-baseline-frozen-worktree 2026-10-15 02:52:55, r81-frozen 2026-10-15 03:37:59 vs wt-r98 2026-10-16 05:43:07, wt-r99 05:43:13, wt-r100 05:43:18. Verified: --expire '2026-10-16T00:00:00' and '2026-10-15T12:00:00' and '2026-10-16 00:00:00' -> removes ONLY r80/r81; --expire '1 day ago' / '2 days ago' / 'now' -> removes all five.
mechanism_c_expire_window.warning: This split is an INCIDENTAL property of file mtimes, not an operator guarantee: any touch of a pin's admin dir (or of its gitdir file) collapses it, and git's --expire grammar is loose ('@2026-10-16' silently pruned all five, i.e. it did NOT behave like the timestamp form). NOT-SAFE to rely on. Prefer mechanism A (lock) or B (remove-by-path).

mechanism_d_backup_and_restore.command: cp -a .git/worktrees/<name> <safe-dir> before pruning, restore after; or `git worktree repair` if a worktree dir is recreated
mechanism_d_backup_and_restore.effect: A copy of the admin dir preserves the registration and its index/ORIG_HEAD/reflog; a plain `git worktree prune` then removes the originals and the copies can be moved back.
mechanism_d_backup_and_restore.empirically_verified: NO — not exercised in this seat (it writes outside the fragment and outside a mktemp fixture). Recorded as a fallback only; the exact restore semantics were not verified, so treat as to-verify.
